title: Suomi on maailman onnellisin mutta myös maailman vapain maa
content:
Jos Euroviisuissa tai jääkiekossa ei tule menestystä, ei hätää: meillä suomalaisilla on silti aihetta juhlaan.

Saatoit ehkä törmätä maaliskuussa uutiseen Maailman onnellisuusraportista, jonka mukaan Suomi oli jo yhdeksättä vuotta peräkkäin maailman onnellisin maa.

Vähemmälle huomiolle jäi toinen mairitteleva tulos, joka julkistettiin samana päivänä: Freedom Housen mukaan Suomi on myös maailman vapain maa.

Freedom House arvioi valtioiden vapautta yhteensä 25 eri kysymyksellä, jotka koskevat esimerkiksi vaalijärjestelmää, oikeuslaitoksen toimintaa, sananvapautta ja kokoontumisvapautta. Kunkin kysymyksen osalta maat pisteytetään asteikolla 0–4, joten vapauden kokonaisskaala ulottuu nollasta sataan.

Suomi on maailman ainoa maa, joka saa täydet sata pistettä. Eikä siinä vielä kaikki: Suomi on saanut täydet pisteet joka vuosi siitä lähtien, kun Freedom House otti käyttöön nykyisen pisteytyksen vuoden 2014 raportissa.

title: Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions over Red Sea port have turned the Tigray peace deal into a political weapon
content:
The large-scale war between the Ethiopian federal government and Tigray regional government forces ended in November 2022 with the signing of the Pretoria Agreement. The two sides agreed that the Tigrayan forces would disarm, and that foreign forces and other troops outside the federal army would withdraw from Tigray. They also agreed to restore constitutional order in Tigray and resolve disputes over contested areas in accordance with the constitution.

I study armed conflict, governance and political communication in Ethiopia. I recently analysed the Pretoria Agreement and its implementation. I examined official statements from Ethiopian, Eritrean and Tigrayan authorities, reports by international organisations and conflict monitors, and news reports published between November 2022 and June 2026. This enabled me to trace how disputes over disarmament, territory and political representation became connected to the rivalry between landlocked Ethiopia and Eritrea over access to the Red Sea.

I found that while the Pretoria Agreement remains accepted by the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), its main commitments have been applied selectively.

title: Elga Sesemannin näyttely Ateneumissa imee mukaansa
content:
Eero Karisto

Elga Sesemann on ennestäänkin tuttu Ateneumin kävijöille. Monille hänet muistaville lienee jäänyt mieleen räiskyvä ellei peräti räiskivä palettiveitsen käyttö. Maalia on paksusti ja ääriviivat häilyviä. Sesemannia onkin luonnehdittu 1940-luvulta lähtien merkittäväksi ekspressionistiksi ja suomalaisen modernin taiteen omaperäiseksi uudistajaksi.

Näyttelyssä huomaa, että oli hän paljon muutakin. Mukana on erilaisia tekniikkoja, esittävää ja enemmän tai vähemmän abstrakteja töitä. Usein kuvattava kohde on jossain hämyn tai muun taustalla, siellä jossain, ehkä menneisyydessä. Tunnelma on yleensä rauhallinen, poissaoleva, ehkä melankolinen.

Sesemann (1922–2007) piti ensimmäisen oman näyttelynsä 23-vuotiaana, ja sai paljon huomiota ja myös kiitosta, selviää Ateneumin näyttelytiedoista. Häntä on verrattu Edward Munchiin ja Helene Schjerfbeckiin. Sesemannin omakuvat ovatkin lähempänä Schjerfbeckin kuin Eero Nelimarkan runsaita omakuvia, joita on esillä samaan aikaan Nelimarkan näyttelyssä Ateneumissa.

title: LUT-yliopisto sai laatuleiman – LUTin vahvuuksia ovat kunnianhimoinen strateginen ote ja vahva sitoutuminen toiminnan kehittämiseen
content:
Lappeenrannan-Lahden teknillinen yliopisto (LUT) läpäisi Kansallisen koulutuksen arviointikeskuksen (Karvi) kansainvälisen auditointiryhmän toteuttaman auditoinnin. Auditoinnin mukaan LUT panostaa vahvasti tutkimukseen, koulutukseen, opiskelijalähtöiseen oppimiseen, kansainvälisyyteen ja jatkuvaan kehittämiseen. LUT voisi vahvistaa kuitenkin koulutusta systemaattisemmalla seurannalla ja laadunhallinnalla.

Vahva strateginen suunta tukee LUTin kehitystä

title: Digital Silk Road Builds Big Balkan Shadow
content:
Since 2007 in Serbia and 2008 in Albania, Chinese telecom vendors — particularly Huawei — have expanded across the Balkans, deploying 3G and 4G telecommunications infrastructure, as well as Chinese-built surveillance networks.

But both countries, plus North Macedonia, also promised to limit Chinese 5G involvement.  The US and Europe consider Chinese telecom vendors a security risk. This May, the US Export-Import Bank approved financing this year for Telekom Srbija’s 5G rollout, contingent on the operator using US equipment.

Will the recent US move limit Chinese influence in the Western Balkans, a term invented by the European Union to describe the six Balkan countries in Southeast Europe seeking EU membership, work? My analysis suggests no. The countries will remain addicted to Chinese tech.

title: UN chief tells countries to rein in autonomous weapons
content:
BRUSSELS — Countries should ban or restrict the use of autonomous weaponry, United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said on Tuesday, in a joint appeal with the Red Cross.

The world is inching closer to “crossing a moral red line”, the “autonomous targeting of humans by machines,” Guterres said. The UN press release referred to “unconfirmed reports” that drones guided by artificial intelligence are being deployed on the battlefield.

On Monday, the New York Times ran a story which claimed that a Russian AI-guided drone killed three Ukrainians, highlighting how AI could evolve drone warfare.

Guterres and ICRC chief Mirjana Spoljaric underlined that targeting civilians in war is a violation of international humanitarian law, and said they fear that machines won’t be able to tell the difference between combatants and non-combatants.

Both called for a ban on autonomous weapons which produce unpredictable results and anti-personnel weapons that deliberately target human beings.

title: Türkiye: European Court Orders Rights Defender’s Immediate Release
content: (London, August 25, 2026) – The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights today delivered a landmark judgment in the case of Osman Kavala, the human rights defender and civil society leader unlawfully imprisoned in Türkiye since November 2017. The court ruled that Kavala's continued detention is unlawful and found that his rights to fair trial, freedom of expression, and association have been violated. The court also found that his aggravated life sentence amounts to inhuman and degrading treatment and that the Turkish authorities acted in bad faith by keeping him in detention unlawfully. The court concluded that he was convicted for the ulterior purpose of punishing and silencing him, and to prevent his human rights work. The court ordered his release at the earliest possible date and that his conviction be quashed.

title: Kazakhstan’s Election Brings a New Parliament — and More Pressure on Journalists
content:
Kazakhstan’s first election to a new unicameral Parliament on Sunday gave a commanding victory to the newly formed, pro-presidential Adilet, or “Justice,” party, in a vote that press-freedom advocates said was held amid mounting pressure on independent journalists.

Adilet won 71.17 percent of the vote, or about 6.5 million ballots, while turnout was 74 percent, according to results released Tuesday by Kazakhstan’s Central Election Commission. Four other parties cleared the five-percent threshold.

None of the seven parties that took part in the election could be seen as opposing President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s policies, according to international observers.

The new 145-seat legislative body is elected entirely through a proportional representation system based on party lists.

The new unicameral Parliament, called the Kurultai, was established earlier this year following constitutional reforms promoted by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. It replaced Kazakhstan’s former two-chamber parliament, abolishing the upper house and the mixed electoral system under which voters could also choose candidates directly, rather than only from party lists.

title: Left-handed people tend to be left-leaning voters
content:
Political preferences are generally explained by income, age and level of education. However, our research suggests that a far more unexpected trait may also have a hand in how we vote. A survey carried out in 18 western countries has shown that left-handed people tend to identify more strongly with the political left. This findings appear to be more related to identity than biology.

Our research shows that a statistical link actually exists between being left-handed and holding left-leaning political views.

In a recent study carried out as part of our academic research, we set out to determine whether a characteristic as commonplace as which hand we write with could be linked to political views.

To find out, we surveyed 1,404 people across 18 Western countries, including France, Germany, the United States, Italy and Spain. Participants indicated their political stance on a ten-point scale ranging from right to left, as well as which hand they write with. We then compared their answers, taking into account numerous factors such as age, income, gender and level of education.

title: Waymo to launch robotaxis in Munich in 2027
content:
Waymo will introduce its self-driving taxis in Munich by the end of 2027, the American autonomous driving company announced today.

The Google subsidiary will start rolling out vehicles in the German city this year, which will be manually driven while the company “starts with high-definition mapping of local street networks” and testing with safety drivers, Waymo said in a statement.

“Bavaria is determined to live up to its pioneering role and be an international leader in autonomous driving,” Florian Herrmann, the head of the Bavarian state chancellery, said in the statement. “Now we need to move quickly from testing to real-world deployment.” 

The news marks Waymo’s first foray into the European Union. It already operates in 11 cities in the United States and has applied for a license in the United Kingdom to launch its robotaxis in London this year.

Earlier this month, London transport authorities approved the licenses of fellow American company Uber and British firm Wayve to start testing a small number of their autonomous vehicles.

title: Mexico: Fix ‘Rights of Audiences’ Regulation
content:
(Mexico City) ­– Mexico’s government has proposed regulations on “rights of audiences” that pose a threat to freedom of expression, Human Rights Watch said today.

On July 28, 2026, the government announced a draft regulation that, if issued, would grant the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission—a body under the executive branch—broad powers to fine media outlets that publish allegedly “false,” “decontextualized,” or “outdated” information.

“Accuracy is a cornerstone of responsible journalism, but the government should not be in charge of deciding whether media outlets are doing their job well,” said Jorge Peniche, senior Mexico researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The Mexican government should revise this draft of administrative rules to ensure it does not threaten free speech and independent media.”

title: Türkiye: Long Prison Terms for Children Accused of Crime
content:
(Berlin) – A new Turkish law that imposes heavy prison sentences on children found guilty of committing crimes is likely to cause harm and moves Turkish policy further away from international norms, Human Rights Watch said today. The law, which went into effect on August 18, 2026, allows courts to impose prison sentences up to 27 years for children age 12 and up, and life in prison for those 15 and older.

Imposing criminal penalties on children younger than 14 and sentencing children as though they were adults violates international child rights standards. The law also directs officials to hold children in closed prisons and not in educational facilities, as is the appropriate practice for child offenders. Türkiye should instead reform its child justice system to comply with the best international standards.

title: Leap forward in European Web sovereignty: Horizon Europe funded project “OpenWebSearch.EU” ends after 42 months and puts forth a federated Open Web Index pilot I Media Release
content:
Passau / Munich — August 2026

The OpenWebSearch.EU consortium announced the successful completion of its 42 months long Horizon Europe funded project, having built and validated a first federated European Open Web Index (OWI). The project results include technical, economic and operational evidence that an Open Web Index can strengthen Europe’s digital sovereignty and support research, innovation and trustworthy AI.

  • Creation of an operational Open Web Index: ~39 billion URLs crawled across 185 languages, 28 million hosts, producing a 45 TiB web-index from 1.25 PiB of raw data
  • Data availability and tooling for research and R&D, publishing 1,511 public datasets and providing data shards via the OpenWebIndex.eu portal for research use
  • Proof of a federated public–private infrastructure approach that can be scaled with further funding and additional infrastructure partners
  • Commissioned market potential study (MRC, 2024) projecting a net benefit of ~€4.5 billion over 10 years and an expected return on investment within four years of operation
  • Delivery of multiple use case projects on top of the OWI (e.g., OMMS for map POI enrichment)

title: Gulahallat – Encounters with Contemporary Sámi Art
content:
Institut finlandais presents Gulahallat – Encounters with Contemporary Sámi Art, an exhibition bringing together works by leading Sámi artists alongside a selection of traditional Sámi handicrafts. The exhibition is organised in partnership with Oulu 2026 European Capital of Culture. It features artworks from the collections of the Rovaniemi Art Museum, as well as the Sámi Museum Siida located in Aanaar/Inari in Sápmi, the Sámi homeland area. In Northern Sámi, Gulahallat refers to dialogue, to mutual understanding, and to being heard.

The exhibition showcases the work of nine contemporary Sámi artists: Tomas Colbengtson, Marja Helander, Niillas Holmberg, Jouni S. Laiti, Hildá Länsman, Tomas Magnusson, Outi Pieski, Lada Suomenrinne and Liselotte Wajstedt. They live across Sápmi, some on the Finnish and some on the Swedish side, reflecting the fact that Sámi art transcends not only artistic disciplines but also the borders of the Nordic states. Their works – photography, film, textiles and traditional handicrafts – combine ancestral techniques with contemporary artistic practices.

title: 2.10 HOW-oppimisympäristö & Utopia vai dystopia -kierros
content:
HOW-oppimisympäristö & Utopia vai dystopia -kierros, Tommi Rikkinen, Tekniikan museo (Viikintie 1, 00560 Helsinki)

Tässä tapahtumassa tutustutaan Tekniikan museon HOW-oppimisympäristöön, jossa luonnontieteet, matematiikka ja teknologia yhdistyvät tekemällä ja kokeilemalla oppimiseen. HOW koostuu toiminnallisista työpisteistä, joissa tutkitaan muun muassa energiaa, materiaaleja, teknologiaa ja kestävää tulevaisuutta. Oppimisympäristön lähtökohtana on ajatus oppimisesta tekemällä, kokeilemalla ja yhdessä oivaltamalla. Työpisteet on tuotettu lukuisten yhteistyökumppanien kanssa.

Tämän jälkeen siirrytään keskustelevalle Utopia vai dystopia -kierrokselle, jossa tarkastellaan teknologian mahdollisuuksia ja uhkia. Miten tekoäly, robotiikka ja muu teknologinen kehitys muuttavat ihmisten arkea ja yhteiskuntaa? Milloin teknologia auttaa meitä – ja milloin se alkaa määrittää elämäämme liikaa? Kierros tarjoaa näkökulmia tulevaisuuteen ja haastaa pohtimaan yksilön roolia maailmassa.

title: Kirjastolehden syysnumero tilattavissa
content:
Vaikka ympäröivä maailma on mullistusten pyörteissä, kirjastoon voi luottaa. Sieltä löytyvät sivistys, lukemisen nautinto ja ystävällinen asiakaspalvelu. Emme välttämättä aina arjessa edes muista, miten tärkeä palvelu kirjasto on suomalaisille. Kirjastolehden tehtävänä on muistuttaa kirjaston tärkeydestä ja vahvistaa kirjastorakkautta.

Kirjastolehden syysnumero ilmestyy 23.9.2026. Tilaamalla asiakaslehdet 16.9.2026 mennessä varmistat, että lehti on kirjastossasi julkaisupäivänä valmiina jaettavaksi.

Kirjastolehti kertoo asiakkaille innostavasti kirjaston arjesta. Syysnumerossamme puhutaan sivareiden muuttuvasta roolista kirjastossa, kirjastojen tarjoamasta epävirallisesta digitaalisesta hoivasta ja digitoinnista pelastamassa kirjallisuutta.

title: NERDS (North European Resonance and Dissonance Society)
content:
Nätverkets främsta mål är att främja informationsutbyte och kunskapsutbyte om varandras experimentella musikscener, att initiera nya samarbeten samt att öka publikens tillgång till nyskapande musikevenemang och artister i den nordisk-baltiska regionen.

NERDS anordnar initiativ och aktiviteter, såsom festivaler, seminarier och workshops. De har även ordnat idémöten för att stärka nödvändiga kompetenser, såsom digitalisering, ekonomisk hållbarhet, kreativitet inom produktion och marknadsföring. Dessa aktiviteter bidrar till en hållbar tillväxt inom den nordisk-baltiska experimentella musikscenen och dess närvaro på den globala arenan. Nätverket håller månatliga onlinemöten för att utbyta information om varje festivals aktiviteter och samordna kommande projekt.

Långvarigt nätverksstöd ingår i det nordisk-baltiska mobilitetsprogrammet för kultur som stärker konstnärligt och kulturellt samarbete i Norden och Baltikum.

Läs mer om nätverksstöd, våra andra stödprogram och ansökningstider här!

Välkommen till en interaktiv och inspirerande förmiddag om svenskan i Finland och Nordjobb! Förmiddagen riktar sig i första hand till lärare på gymnasiet och till studie- och yrkesvägledare.

title: Så stödjer Svenska institutet ukrainska familjer som söker sina försvunna anhöriga
content:
Med stöd från Svenska institutet har en databas byggts upp för att dokumentera försvinnanden och stödja drabbade familjer. Bakom arbetet står svenska Östgruppen för demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter och den ukrainska människorättsorganisationen Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group (KHPG). Databasen innehåller i dag information om närmare 21 000 personer och kan även användas i utredningar och framtida rättsprocesser.

– Många ser bilder på bombningar och förstörda städer, men inte lika många känner till att civila utsätts för påtvingade försvinnanden – vilket ofta följs av tortyr och andra former av omänsklig behandling – eller att familjer inte vet var deras anhöriga finns, säger Ausra Padskocimaite, doktor i folkrätt och projektledare på Östgruppen.

– Dessa handlingar utgör grova kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter och även krigsbrott, fortsätter hon.

Ukrainska myndigheter uppskattar att omkring 16 000 civila har förts bort och hålls olagligt fängslade av Ryssland, men den verkliga siffran kan vara ännu högre. I strid med internationell humanitär rätt döms många i skenrättegångar och hålls under långa perioder utan kontakt med omvärlden.

title: Master’s student, apply for Global Palestine -online course
content:
The Finnish Institute in the Middle East (FIME), in collaboration with Tampere University, is pleased to invite applications for the course Global Palestine: Tracing the Shifting Horizons of Violence and Power (5 ECTS).

The course examines Palestine’s role in global circuits of violence, capital, technology, and politics. It explores the entanglements between global and local processes, colonialism and imperialism, capital and geopolitics, and considers Palestine as a site where these forces are produced, contested, and transformed.

Through an interdisciplinary approach, the course provides conceptual and methodological tools for critically examining the connections between Palestine and wider global processes. Topics include new technologies, war and the environment, academic institutions, political and social movements, military supply chains, capitalist elites, security and surveillance, and emerging forms of everyday life and resistance.

The course brings together leading scholars working across geography, anthropology, political theory, international relations, environmental humanities, and science and technology studies.

title: Ars Electronica Solutions – A Glimpse Behind the Scenes
content:
Ars Electronica Solutions – A Glimpse Behind the Scenes ist ein interaktiver Dialog- und Erfahrungsraum, der Einblicke in die Arbeitsprozesse von Ars Electronica Solutions im Ars Electronica Center gewährt. Hier wird gezeigt, wie aus Ideen, Fragestellungen und technologischen Möglichkeiten innovative Konzepte entstehen und zu konkreten Anwendungen und immersiven Erlebnissen werden – und wie dabei kreative, technische, organisatorische und wirtschaftliche Anforderungen zusammenspielen.

Daraus entstehen Anwendungen, die wissenschaftliche, technologische und gesellschaftliche Entwicklungen anschaulich vermitteln, neue Perspektiven eröffnen und den Austausch fördern. Agentische Systeme begleiten Besucher*innen durch die Ausstellung, reagieren auf ihre Interessen, unterstützen bei der Orientierung und vermitteln Inhalte auf persönliche Weise. Die Ausstellung richtet sich an Jung und Alt, an Neugierige wie an Expert*innen. Sie lädt ein, die Prozesse hinter den Projekten kennenzulernen und zu entdecken, wie Ideen durch Kreativität, Technologie und interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit zu erlebbaren Geschichten werden – Geschichten, die informieren, berühren und inspirieren.

title: New Czech–Swiss Collaboration for Digital Humanities and Language Research: the ELC-DHLR Project
content:
Czech-Swiss Cooperation of CLARIN and DARIAH Infrastructures

We are pleased to announce the launch of Enhancing Library Collections for Digital Humanities and Language Research (ELC-DHLR), a new Czech–Swiss collaborative project that brings together leading research infrastructures and libraries to improve access to and reuse of cultural and linguistic collections for research.

Funded in the framework of the Second Swiss Contribution for Bilateral relations Switzerland–Czech Republic, ELC-DHLR aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Czech and Swiss research infrastructures while advancing the integration of library collections into the European research ecosystem. The project contributes to the broader objective of reinforcing international collaboration in research infrastructures and increasing the visibility, accessibility, and interoperability of digital collections for the arts, humanities, and language sciences.

title: The Daily Routine of Marcus Aurelius: How to Live Like a Stoic
content:
Marcus Aurelius did not have a smartphone. In fact, he didn’t have a phone of any kind, owing to the fact that he lived in the second century, though we can be reasonably certain that he commanded more than enough messengers to keep himself informed around the clock. That’s because he was the Roman emperor at a time when the Roman Empire was at its height. And so, none of us will ever know Marcus’ freedom from digital distraction, nor will we know the intense responsibility he must have felt, no matter how grand a title we attain in our own careers. Still, even here in the twenty-first century, we would all do well to live by the example he left.

So believes Ryan Holiday, a popularizer of Stoicism, the school of thought primarily defined by Marcus’ writings, as well as those of statesman-dramatist Seneca the Younger and former slave Epictetus. In his Meditations, Marcus included enough detail about his own life that Holiday could make the video above for his YouTube channel Daily Stoic, which breaks down the emperor’s daily routine.

title: How a 17th-century Irish law is shielding Big Tech from class actions in Europe
content:
DUBLIN — An obscure 400-year-old Irish law is holding back collective legal action against Big Tech firms in Europe.

For decades, consumers in the United States have been banding together to sue companies for billions of dollars in compensation for harm caused by everything from tobacco and oil to online shopping. Five years ago, Europeans got similar rights to file continent-wide consumer class-action cases against corporations, prompted by the “Dieselgate” emissions scandal that forced German carmaker Volkswagen into a settlement of more than $9.5 billion with U.S. consumers.

But many of the world’s largest tech giants, with millions of users, deep pockets and a track record of breaking EU rules, have so far been spared from major class action challenges. That’s because in Ireland, where many of these firms have their EU headquarters, it is illegal for a funder to finance a legal case unless it is directly involved or has a legitimate interest.

title: Lainvalmistelun prosessiopas: Perus- ja ihmisoikeudet huomioitava
content:
Ihmisoikeusliitto lausui oikeusministeriölle uuden lainvalmistelun prosessioppaan luonnoksesta.

Ihmisoikeusliitto pitää uuden prosessioppaan tavoitteita kannatettavina. Lausunnossa korostetaan, että laadukas, avoin ja osallistava lainvalmistelu on keskeinen osa oikeusvaltiota sekä julkisen vallan velvollisuutta turvata perus- ja ihmisoikeuksien toteutuminen.

Lausunnossa Ihmisoikeusliitto nostaa esiin erityisesti seuraavat näkökulmat:

  • Perustuslain 22 §:n mukainen julkisen vallan velvollisuus turvata perus- ja ihmisoikeuksien toteutuminen tulisi tunnistaa lainvalmistelun yleiseksi lähtökohdaksi.
  • Perus- ja ihmisoikeusvaikutusten arvioinnille tulisi antaa nykyistä näkyvämpi ja systemaattisempi rooli koko lainvalmisteluprosessin ajan.
  • Oppaassa tulisi viitata oikeusministeriön perus- ja ihmisoikeusvaikutusten arviointia koskevaan ohjeistukseen.
  • Kansalaisyhteiskunnan, kansalaisjärjestöjen ja sääntelyn kohteena olevien ihmisryhmien osallistumismahdollisuuksia tulee vahvistaa.
  • Erityistä huomiota tulee kiinnittää niiden ryhmien kuulemiseen, jotka ovat syrjinnän vaarassa tai joiden oikeuksiin sääntely vaikuttaa merkittävästi.

title: Children’s Digital Rights Need More Than a False Promise of Safety
content:
By Lisa Dittmer, Amnesty International’s Children’s Digital Rights Researcher, and Paloma Candia and Ahmed Dhman both Amnesty International’s Digital Rights Champions, a global network of child and youth human rights defenders.

This article was first published in TechPolicy.Press

Children’s online safety has become a leading political issue as concerns about Big Tech harms have moved from academic debates to bestseller lists and mainstream news. French President Emmanuel Macron hailed France’s teen social media ban as “leading the way in Europe in protecting our children and our teenagers.” France’s top court later blocked the law, citing privacy and freedom of expression concerns. United Nations (UN) Secretary-General Guterres has called for an artificial intelligence (AI) Child Safety Pledge. Yet amid the flurry of high-level pledges and the rush to protect “our children,” the voices of one demographic are noticeably absent: children themselves.

title: Poisoned waters: Indigenous communities fight to protect Thailand’s Kok River
content:
Demonstrators held a ‘Peace Walk’ calling for accountability over mining activities affecting rivers and rural communities

Originally published on Global Voices

Communities demand action as Kok River contamination remains unresolved. Photo from Prachatai, content partner of Global Voices.

This edited article by Sheikh Mehzabin Chitra was published by Prachatai, an independent news site in Thailand. An edited version has been republished by Global Voices under a content partnership agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

Hundreds of villagers, Indigenous leaders, environmental defenders, monks, and civil society activists completed a six-day Peace Walk in July along northern Thailand’s Kok River to demand urgent action against worsening water contamination. Their message was clear: The river that has sustained communities for generations is becoming increasingly unsafe, and stronger action is needed to stop transboundary pollution before irreversible damage is done.

title: Colombia: Armed Groups Expand Child Recruitment
content:
(Washington, DC) – Child recruitment by armed groups has increased in Colombia as the government has failed to respond effectively, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today.

Recruitment and Use of Children by Colombian Armed Groups

Download the full report in English

Appendix I: Letter from Meta to Human Rights Watch

Appendix II: Email from TikTok to Human Rights Watch

The 102-page report, “‘I Thought I’d Never See My Mom Again’: Recruitment and Use of Children by Colombian Armed Groups,” examines the dynamics of child recruitment, the factors that place children at risk, and the strategies and tools used by armed groups, including through social media platforms, to recruit them. Researchers also analyzed the government’s response and its shortcomings in preventing child recruitment, protecting and rescuing children, assisting the reintegration of those who have been released, and prosecuting the individuals responsible.

title: Frontline Pacific: Greening The Earth May Pollute The Oceans
content:
By Kalinga Seneviratne *

SYDNEY, Australia | 24 August 2026 (IDN) — In the past year there has been a scramble by the big powers to secure the continuing supply of “rare mineral” that are used in batteries driving electric cars and wind power turbines. There is a looming catastrophe awaiting the Pacific Ocean if countries in the region  are not alert to the environmental threats facing the region.

Decades ago, greedy industrialists were polluting the air, and their government’  refused to listen to scientific warnings of a looming climatic disaster, and now the island nations of the South Pacific is facing the brunt of climate change disasters. If the current trends of digging out “rare minerals” from wherever you can find it continues, we will be left with oceans – especially the Pacific – where we cannot swim or fish in the oceans, further threatening the livelihoods of many small Pacific Island nations.

title: Maksuton kouluruoka on maailmalla yhä harvinaisuus
content:
Tänään 24.8. käynnistyy Suomen World Visionin perinteinen Kouluruokakampanja, jonka suojelijana toimii ruoka-alan moniosaaja Teresa Välimäki.

Kampanja muistuttaa kouluruuan merkityksestä ja kerää varoja kouluruokailun tukemiseen kehittyvissä maissa.

Maailmalla maksuton kouluruoka on yhä harvinaisuus. Erityisesti näin on matalan tulotason maissa, joissa vain 27 prosenttia alakoululaisista saa maksuttoman tai tuetun kouluruuan.

– Suomessa kouluruuan merkitys hyvinvoinnin ja tasa-arvon rakentamisessa on ollut suuri ja on sitä yhä. Toivoisin, että sama mahdollisuus avautuisi kaikille lapsille, Teresa Välimäki sanoo.

Hän vierailee syyskuun alussa Ruandassa tutustumassa Suomen World Visionin kouluruokatyöhön.

– Haluan olla mukana tukemassa kouluruokailua, sillä se on tehokas tapa lisätä lasten hyvinvointia ja vähentää köyhyyttä.

Ravitsevan kouluruuan merkitys lasten terveydelle ja oppimistuloksille on selvä. Kouluruoka helpottaa välitöntä nälkää, auttaa jaksamaan ja tukee keskittymistä.

Kouluruuan positiiviset vaikutukset kantavat pitkälle. Lähellä tuotettu kouluruoka luo työpaikkoja ja tuloja. Lisäksi se tukee tyttöjen pääsyä kouluun.

– Kouluruoka tuo turvaa lasten arkeen. Äärimmäisessä köyhyydessä eläville kouluruoka voi olla päivän ainut varma ateria, Suomen World Visionin ohjelmajohtaja Christina Nyback sanoo.

Suomen World Vision kampanjoi kouluruuan puolesta 24.8.–30.9. ja kerää varoja kouluruokailun tukemiseen nälästä kärsivillä alueilla.

title: Johda kasvua, joka muuttaa maailmaa – hae YK:n tasa-arvojärjestö UN Women Suomen varainhankinnan päälliköksi
content:
Haluatko johtaa yhden Suomen tunnetuimman tasa-arvojärjestön varainhankintaa ja kasvattaa sen vaikuttavuutta? UN Women Suomi hakee varainhankinnan päällikköä rakentamaan uusia mahdollisuuksia naisten ja tyttöjen oikeuksien edistämiseksi. Tehtävää yhdistää strategisen ajattelun, kunnianhimoiset kasvutavoitteet ja merkityksellisen yhteiskunnallisen vaikuttavuuden. Positio tarjoaa sinulle ainutlaatuisen mahdollisuuden vaikuttaa siihen, miten yhä useampi ihminen, yritys ja yhteisö voi olla mukana rakentamassa tasa-arvoisempaa maailmaa.

Oletko johtanut kuukausilahjoittajapainotteista yksityisvarainhankintaa ja tehnyt tulosta? Tarjoamme sen, mitä harva pystyy: aidon johtoryhmäpaikan, koko yksityisvarainhankinnan omistajuuden, tunnetun ja pidetyn brändin sekä UN Womenin kansainvälisen asiantuntijaverkoston tuen.

Varainhankintamme ja tunnettuutemme on kolminkertaistunut tällä vuosikymmenellä. Haluamme kasvattaa kuukausilahjoittamista entisestään sekä rakentaa samalla uusia tulovirtoja. Sinä johdat tätä työtä.

title: Europol Warns of Violent Shift in European Museum Heists
content:
Europol is warning of an alarming shift in museum heists across Europe, as criminal networks abandon traditional stealth in favor of brute force and extreme violence, according to a report published Monday.

The European Union’s law enforcement agency said perpetrators are increasingly ditching the traditional “deception and discreet execution” of art theft, historically viewed as a “non-violent form of organized property crime,” in favor of direct and confrontational methods.

Instead of niche experts, Europol’s report—”Changing Tactics, Changing Targets: The Evolving Nature of Museum Heists”—found that these new heists are often carried out by decentralized groups of opportunistic criminals recruited via social media on a “crime-as-a-service” basis. These new criminal profiles are increasingly armed with sledgehammers, axes, crowbars, and explosives and firearms to breach premises, smash display cases and intimidate or assault staff in broad daylight.

title: His Research on Pregnant Opioid Users Was Widely Celebrated. Auditors and Experts Found Major Flaws.
content:
When Dr. Craig Towers moved to Knoxville, Tennessee, in 2010, the high-risk obstetrician encountered a crisis unlike anything he’d seen.

Towers, who had practiced for 25 years in California and Wisconsin, found himself caring for an unusual number of pregnant women addicted to painkillers — and delivering newborns who were suffering withdrawal symptoms. Those babies, born shaking and inconsolable and who required weeks of specialized care, were becoming tragic symbols of the region’s raging opioid epidemic. “We were inundated,” Towers later told the Knoxville News Sentinel.

In those initial years in Tennessee, Towers recognized a need — and a research opportunity.

title: Suomalainen taide ei voi vaikuttaa, jos sitä ei voi nähdä
content:
Suomessa on tehty valtava työ museoiden kokoelmien digitoinnissa. Kokoelmia on kuvattu, luetteloitu ja avattu digitaaliseen käyttöön vuosien ajan. Silti suomalaisen kuvataiteen näkyvyys verkossa riippuu edelleen liian usein siitä, löytyykö teosten tekijänoikeuskorvauksiin rahoitusta.

Museot kyllä haluaisivat tuoda kokoelmansa yleisön nähtäville. Monet taidemuseot ovat tehneet Kuvaston kanssa sopimuksen, joka mahdollistaa teosten esittämisen verkossa ja tekijänoikeuskorvausten maksamisen taiteilijoille. Yhteistyössä museoiden kanssa myös lupahinnastoa on kehitetty niin, että mahdollisimman monella toimijalla olisi mahdollisuus avata kokoelmiaan verkkoon yleisölle.

Silti osa digitoidusta kulttuuriperinnöstä jää edelleen pimentoon.

Tämä on kulttuuripoliittinen paradoksi. Yhteiskunta investoi taidekokoelmien digitointiin, mutta kaikkia digitoituja aineistoja ei pystytä tuomaan yleisön saataville. Lopputuloksena taiteilijat jäävät ilman korvausta, museot ilman toivottua näkyvyyttä ja yleisö ilman pääsyä osaan yhteisestä kulttuuriperinnöstämme.

title: Volodymyr Zelensky’s other war: Ukraine’s endless struggle with corruption
content:
Ukraine celebrated this year’s independence day on August 24 in the presence of key allies and amid the unfolding of another major corruption scandal.

It all started when Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine’s defence minister until his dismissal as part of a government reshuffle last month, posted a nine-minute video on August 19 that was widely seen as a direct challenge to the country’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky. One part of the challenge was what amounted to a call for an election, despite the fact that the ballot would have to be held in wartime. This is something that both Zelensky and a majority of Ukrainians have repeatedly rejected.

The other part of Fedorov’s challenge was his diagnosis of a “systemic crisis of governance”. He is not wrong. Corruption in Ukraine is no longer simply about this scandal or that minister. It is a pattern of elite behaviour that has outlasted every Ukrainian government since independence. It survived revolutions in 2004 and 2014 fought explicitly in the name of ending it. And it’s now undermining a war for national survival.

Hossam Ghazylle kysymys on helppo. Hän aikoo viettää viimeiset vuotensa synnyinmaassaan Egyptissä ja tulla haudatuksi sinne.

Omar Abuzaidille kuolinpaikan valinta on ristiriitaisempaa. Hän on syntyjään palestiinalainen mutta vietti lapsuutensa Jordaniassa ja opiskeli Saksassa. Euroopassa hän on elänyt jo 40 vuotta, joista valtaosan Suomessa. Täällä ovat myös lapset ja lapsenlapset.

”Ehkäpä minä jään Suomeen.”

Suomeen on tullut ihmisiä maailmalta aina, mutta isossa kuvassa maahanmuuttohistoriamme on varsin lyhyt. Suurin osa ulkomaalaistaustaisista ihmisistä on saapunut Suomeen 1990-luvulla ja sen jälkeen. Siirtolaistaustaisten ihmisten ikääntyminen onkin meillä varsin uusi ilmiö.

title: Tutkimus: luontohaittojen hyvitysten koko vaihtelee jopa tuhatkertaisesti
content:
Samankokoinen luontohaitta voi vaatia jopa tuhatkertaisesti erisuuruisen hyvitysalueen riippuen siitä, missä ja miten luontoa ennallistetaan, paljastaa Helsingin yliopiston uusi tutkimus.

Puron pieni rumpuputki voi estää kalojen ja muiden vesieliöiden liikkumisen. Kun putki poistetaan, luonto toipuu usein nopeasti ja varmasti. Karu mäntykangas on toista maata: jätettynä oman onnensa nojaan sen palautuminen voi kestää vuosisatoja. 

Tämä ero on yksi ekologisen kompensaation haasteista. Kun rakentaminen tai muu maankäyttö heikentää luontoa jossain, ekologisessa kompensaatiossa haitta korvataan tuottamalla vastaava määrä luontohyötyjä muualla. Koska ennallistaminen on epävarmempaa ja hitaampaa kuin luonnon tuhoaminen, hyvitysalueen täytyy tavallisesti olla heikennysaluetta laajempi. Tätä eroa kuvataan kompensaatiokertoimella. 

"Useimmissa maissa käytössä on yksi tai muutama kiinteä kerroin kaikille elinympäristöille", avaa tutkimusta johtanut Joel Jalkanen Helsingin yliopistosta.  

"Tämä on ongelmallista, sillä elinympäristöt palautuvat niin eri tavoin, että yhden kertoimen käyttö johtaa käytännössä useimmiten luonnon kokonaisheikennykseen", hän jatkaa.

title: Syksyn tapahtumat jatkavat kaupunginkirjaston juhlavuotta!
content:
Lahden kaupunginkirjaston juhlavuoden vietto jatkuu syksyn tapahtumien siivittämissä kohtaamisissa. Luvassa on laaja kattaus keskustelevia tapahtumia ihmisyydestä, yhteiskunnasta ja kirjastosta.


Lahden kirjastojen syksyn 2026 tapahtumateemana jatkuu Lahden kaupunginkirjasto 150 vuotta. Kirjastolla on kyky kannatella elämän koko kirjoa, ja syksyn tapahtumissa käsitellään niin kuolemaa kuin uusien teosten syntyä. Tapahtumat kutsuvat mukaan kaikenikäiset kävijät, nuorimmista ikärikkaisiin.

Juhlavuoden kunniaksi kirjasto keskustelee, kohtaa ja muistelee.

Erätaukokeskustelua käydään monessa muodossa: Nastolan kirjaston Hyvä kuolema jakaa ajatuksia kuoleman kohtaamisesta ja ihmisyydestä. Pääkirjaston Musakirjastomuistoja johdattelee nostalgiamatkalle muistelemaan ja pohtimaan kirjaston musiikkiosaston merkitystä. Keskustelua käydään pääkirjastolla myös paneelikeskustelussa taiteen ja teknologian murroksesta, jossa tarkastellaan tekoälyn haasteita sekä ihmisen korvaamatonta kykyä kertoa ja luoda.

title: Gulahallat – Rencontres avec l’art contemporain sámi
content:
L’Institut finlandais présente l’exposition Gulahallat – Rencontres avec l’art contemporain sámi qui rassemble des œuvres d’artistes majeurs et une sélection d’artisanat, en partenariat avec la Capitale européenne de la culture Oulu 2026. Elle présente des œuvres issues des collections du Musée d’art de Rovaniemi, ainsi que du Musée sámi Siida, situé à Aanaar/Inari, en Sápmi, la région d’origine des Samis. En same du Nord, Gulahallat fait référence au dialogue, à la compréhension et au fait d’être entendu.

Cette exposition met en lumière les œuvres de neuf artistes sámis : Tomas Colbengtson, Marja Helander, Niillas Holmberg, Jouni S. Laiti, Hildá Länsman, Tomas Magnusson, Outi Pieski, Lada Suomenrinne et Liselotte Wajstedt. Ils vivent à travers la région de Sápmi, certains du côté finlandais et d’autres du côté suédois, reflétant le fait que l’art sámi dépasse les frontières non seulement entre pratiques artistiques, mais aussi entre États nordiques. Leurs productions — photographies, films, textiles et pièces artisanales — allient techniques ancestrales et contemporaines.

PEDAALI TIEN PÄÄLLÄ

Haluaisitteko tuoda oman alueenne museotoimijat yhteen inspiroivaan ja käytännönläheiseen työpajaan? Nyt siihen on loistava mahdollisuus!

Pedaali lähtee tien päälle ja etsii yhteistyökumppaneita maakunnista 2–3 tunnin mittaiseen työpajatilaisuuteen, joka järjestetään marraskuussa-tammikuussa erikseen sovittavana ajankohtana. Työpajassa syvennytään asiakkaiden kohtaamiseen museotyössä sekä jaetaan ja kehitetään uusia ja jo toimiviksi todettuja käytäntöjä.

Mitä luvassa?

  • Pedaalin uusien kuvatukikorttien esittely ja kokeilu
  • Vinkkejä siihen, missä ja miten kuvatukikortteja voi hyödyntää omassa työssä
  • Verkostoitumista ja kollegoiden tapaamista
  • Ideoiden jakamista ja yhteistä kehittämistä

title: Discover Deep Space
content:
Der Deep Space 8K von Ars Electronica verbindet hochauflösende Projektionen auf Wand und Boden mit 3D-Darstellungen und interaktiven Anwendungen zu einem immersiven Erlebnisraum. Auf Basis langjähriger Erfahrung entwickelt Ars Electronica Solutions dieses Prinzip kontinuierlich weiter und überträgt es auf unterschiedliche Inhalte, räumliche Situationen und internationale Standorte. Discover Deep Space macht diese Möglichkeiten im Miniaturmodell spielerisch erfahrbar.

Besucher*innen zeichnen eine eigene Skizze, die digital erfasst und Teil der Installation wird. Ein KI-basierter Agent greift die Zeichnung auf, interpretiert sie, stellt Verbindungen zu bestehenden Inhalten her und schlägt passende Anwendungen vor. 
So wird unmittelbar erlebbar, wie aus einer einfachen Idee ein möglicher Ausgangspunkt für ein immersives Erlebnis entsteht – und wie Inhalt, Interaktion und Technologie zusammenspielen, um neue Zugänge zu Wissen und Geschichten zu eröffnen.

title: The Women of the Bauhaus: See Hip, Avant-Garde Photographs of Female Students & Instructors at the Famous Art School
content:
Take a look at photos of Bush Tetras — a three-girl-one-guy No Wave/Post-Punk band from the early 1980s downtown Manhattan scene. Now, look at the photograph above, “Marcel Breuer and His Harem,” by Bauhaus photographer Erich Consemüller, taken sometime around 1927. Except for the fact that Breuer looks more like Ron Mael of Sparks sans mustache than drummer Dee Pop, one might mistake this for a photo of the punk band. This raises a few questions: did art students Bush Tetras look to the women of the Bauhaus for their style? Or did the women of the Bauhaus look to the future and see punk? The second scenario seems more likely since the women of the Bauhaus have not, until recently, been terribly well-known.

I personally feel cheated after studying art and art history in college many years ago and only now getting introduced to several significant artists of the radical German art school founded by Walter Gropius. All of its famous exponents and art stars are men, but it seems the gender ratio of the Bauhaus was closer to that of the general population (as was, in many cases, that of the early punk and post-punk scenes).

title: Support Global Voices Spotlight: Protest in democracy
content:
Protest is a fundamental right, a form of free expression, and a critical means of expressing dissent

Originally published on Global Voices

Global Voices Spotlight: Protest in Democracy. Collage made via Canva. Photos Public Domain.

Protest is a fundamental right, a form of free expression, and a critical means of expressing dissent. Enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, protest is a vital component of democratic societies and a means of addressing societies that are not democratic. Protest has historically helped secure many of the rights we take for granted today — weekends, fair pay, unions, women’s right to vote, and many more. 

Despite the legal basis for the right to protest and its importance to functioning governance, peaceful protest is often curtailed or prohibited, and protesters are painted as illegitimate. Environmental protestors are vilified as “eco-terrorists,” racial justice protestors are derided as “thugs” or “anarchists,” and government critics are dismissed as unpatriotic “foreign agents.”

title: Bangladesh: End Indefinite Pretrial Detention of Political Opponents
content:
(London) – Bangladeshi authorities should immediately take steps to end the prolonged pretrial detention of politicians and others linked to the deposed Awami League government, Human Rights Watch said today. Police detained thousands of party officials, activists, and supporters after Sheikh Hasina was forced to step down as prime minister in August 2024 following weeks of protests, and hundreds remain in prison without being charged with any crime.

Though some officials may have been complicit in the Hasina government’s serious rights violations, many were arrested without apparent evidence on allegations of murdering protesters. Their family members and lawyers allege that the detainees, many of them older people, some with serious health conditions, have been denied basic rights including bail and medical care. At least 10 Awami League office holders, most of whom were not charged with any crime, have died in prison since Prime Minister Tarique Rahman took office in February 2026.

title: Philippines Arrests South Korean Woman Over Alleged $3.9B Online Gambling Operation
content:
Philippine immigration authorities have arrested a 29-year-old South Korean woman wanted in her home country for allegedly helping operate 23 illegal online gambling websites that generated about 5.33 trillion won ($3.9 billion), the country’s Bureau of Immigration said.

Kim Youngsun was detained on August 7 in General Trias, Cavite, in an operation coordinated with South Korean authorities and the Philippine National Police. The Incheon District Court issued a warrant for her arrest in April 2025, and Interpol published a Red Notice two months later. Authorities allege that Kim worked as an assistant manager and supervised several units of the gambling operation, which was run from offices in Pasay and Quezon City beginning in 2018. She is being held at the Bureau of Immigration’s Warden Facility pending custodial proceedings.

OCCRP asked the Philippine Bureau of Immigration to forward a request for comment to Kim but had not received a response by the time of publication.

title: They Rebuilt After Texas’ Devastating Floods. Then Their Home Flooded Again.
content:
When deadly flooding swept through the Texas Hill Country in July of last year, Joan Connor and her husband swam and waded out of their home, surviving only by clinging to a pergola in their front yard. 

The Guadalupe River flood destroyed most of their possessions. It killed at least 119 people in Kerr County, where the couple live, about 100 miles west of Austin. 

But Connor, now 82, and her husband, now 99, moved back into the refurbished house by Christmas, with donated furniture arranged by volunteer decorators. 

They didn’t fear another flood. Connor told me earlier this year: “We don’t think a thing like that will happen again in our lifetime.”

Last month, almost exactly one year after the last deluge, their house flooded again.

I cover climate for The Texas Tribune. I spent months working with ProPublica’s Lexi Churchill and Pratheek Rebala to understand how Texas lawmakers missed dozens of opportunities over nearly 60 years to protect residents in flood-prone places.

title: The law of the innocents: Ireland’s medieval precursor to the Geneva conventions
content:
The Geneva conventions, which were signed in August 1949 in the aftermath of the horrors of the second world war, are generally accepted as the gold standard of international humanitarian law. They set the rules for the treatment of both combatants and civilians during wartime. But they were preceded by more than 12 centuries by a law drawn up by a monk amid the violence of seventh-century Ireland.

Adomnán, the Abbott of Iona, the great Columban island monastery off the western Scottish coast, was a man of many talents. Noted for his biography of St Columba, he was a scholar, teacher, mentor, poet, calendarist and negotiator. He was also known for his efforts to obtain legal guarantees from Pictish, British and Irish kings granting protection from violence to women, children, clerics and others, especially in wartime.

Conflict was commonplace in early medieval Britain and Ireland, we know that much from contemporary written sources, such as the Annals of Tigernach, Bede’s Ecclesiastical History of England and the Chronicon Scotorum. Civilian populations routinely ended up on the receiving end of military violence.

“Demokratia. Oikeusvaltio. Ihmisoikeudet. Tasa-arvo. Ihmisen vapaus päättää omasta elämästään. Niistä meidän on pidettävä kiinni juuri silloin, kun maailma ympärillämme muuttuu nopeasti”, toteaa ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen suurlähettiläskokouksen puheessaan.

Muutokset puhuttaessa mahdollisia

Arvoisat suurlähettiläät ja edustustojen päälliköt, hyvät kollegat,

”Ne, jotka luopuvat olennaisesta vapaudestaan tavoitellakseen vähäistä ja väliaikaista turvallisuutta, eivät ansaitse sen enempää vapautta kuin turvallisuuttakaan.”

Näin kirjoitti Benjamin Franklin.

Franklin oli kirjailija, tiedemies, valtiomies – ja diplomaatti. Hänen ajatuksensa on yli kahden vuosisadan takaa, mutta juuri nyt se tuntuu poikkeuksellisen ajankohtaiselta.

Turvallisuus ilman vapautta ei lopulta ole turvallisuutta. Ja vapaus ilman kykyä puolustaa sitä ei säily.

Siksi Suomen ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikan tärkein päämäärä on lopulta hyvin yksinkertainen:

Suomen vapauden ja kansalaisten hyvinvoinnin turvaaminen.

Tätä tehtävää haluan tänään tarkastella sekä menneen että tulevan kautta.

Kuusilehdon kodissa maalämpö on ollut käytössä talon rakentamisesta eli vuodesta 2007 lähtien. Alkuperäinen ratkaisu oli hieman tavallisuudesta poikkeava Karhu KIV 10 -järjestelmä, jossa maalämpöpumppu ja ilmanvaihtokone oli rakennettu samaan laitekokonaisuuteen.

title: Bloodworth | Accessible AI in the Archives: Tools and Methods for Small Repositories | Archival Issues
content: Abstract:  With ever-expanding digital and digitized holdings, archivists must adopt new methods of processing collections for increased discoverability and accessibility. Artificial intelligence provides one possible solution for meeting the demands of increasingly digital-based archival work. This article fills a gap in existing literature surrounding the potential for AI assistance in descriptive work of digitized handwritten documents by presenting a case study of the use of two AI tools, Transkribus and ChatGPT, for the transcription and improved description of an existing collection of World War II correspondence. Based upon the valuation of these ready-made tools, this study demonstrates the potential usefulness of artificial intelligence for the transcription of digitized handwritten manuscripts and the automation of item-level descriptive tasks to improve accessibility and discoverability of archival materials.

title: Moscow Funds Pro-Kremlin Influence Hub in Belarus
content:
A Moscow-funded cultural center in Minsk has operated as an ideological influence hub for the Kremlin, using hundreds of thousands of dollars in Russian state funds to promote the “Russian world” ideology and cement Moscow’s grip over Belarus, according to leaked internal documents.

The cache of more than 270,000 emails from the Moscow House of Compatriots - obtained by Danish public broadcaster DR and analyzed by OCCRP’s Belarusian member center Buro Media - reveals the scale of Russia’s soft-power spending in its neighbor’s capital.

The House of Moscow in Minsk is the Belarusian branch of the Moscow House of Compatriots, a Russian state organization that works with Russian-speaking communities abroad. Although conceived as a business bridge between Moscow and Minsk, it instead hosted events promoting Russian language, joint historical identity, and Kremlin geopolitical priorities.

These efforts mirror Russia’s so-called “humanitarian policy abroad” - a foreign policy doctrine approved by President Vladimir V. Putin that emphasizes defending the ideals of Russkiy Mir, or the “Russian world,” and countering what Moscow labels “Russophobia.”

title: The free EU database that tells you if an appliance is actually green
content:
When something breaks down, like a washing machine or television, you might find yourself in a showroom or flicking through 12 browser tabs, trying to choose between “eco-friendly” or “green” replacements. They look and cost the same, yet we currently have no way of knowing which claim, if any, is true.

The European Commission has found that more than half of green claims are vague, misleading or unfounded, and four in ten come with no supporting evidence at all. With over 230 sustainability and 100 green energy labels competing for our attention across the EU, no wonder Greenwashing has left consumers and researchers like me trusting none of them.

But the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL) is a digital database that provides the hard evidence needed to cut through the noise.

Since 2019, any appliance requiring an EU energy label – washing machines, fridges, dishwashers, even tyres – must have its performance data logged in a public database before it can be sold. Over 2 million products are now registered.

Here’s how to tap into that database the next time you’re in that showroom.

Katrina – en musikteater är en stark och gripande musikteater som bygger på Sally Salminens klassiska roman från 1936 med samma namn. Verket skildrar den österbottniska bondflickan Katrina som gifter sig med en åländsk sjöman och flyttar till det hårda skärgårdslivet på Åland.

Vid detta gästspel presenteras en särskilt framtagen kammarversion för solister och piano. Manusbearbetning och regi för denna kortare version står Ida Kronholm för. Musiken är komponerad av den åländske tonsättaren Jack Mattsson, som även skrev musiken till den ursprungliga och storskaliga uppsättningen Musikteater Katrina år 1997 för orkester, kör och solister i samband med Ålands 75-årsjubileum av självstyrelsen.

Evenemanget arrangeras av Kulturföreningen Katrina r.f. i samarbete med Finlandsintitutet i Stockholm, Nordens Institut på Åland och Ålands landskapsregering.

title: The Agent
content:
The Agent beinhaltet einen KI-Agenten, der mithilfe eines robotischen Arms agiert. Sie bildet das inhaltliche Herzstück der Ausstellung Ars Electronica Solutions – A Glimpse Behind the Scenes und lädt Besucher*innen dazu ein, einen persönlichen Blick hinter die Kulissen von Ars Electronica Solutions zu werfen. Dabei werden nicht nur fertige Projekte sichtbar, sondern auch die Ideen, Fragen und Arbeitsprozesse, die dahinterstehen. 

Im direkten Dialog mit einem KI-Agenten können Besucher*innen selbst bestimmen, was sie entdecken möchten. Sie können nach einzelnen Projekten fragen, sich in Themen und Technologien vertiefen oder erfahren, wie aus einer ersten Idee ein konkretes Erlebnis entsteht. Der KI-Agent reagiert auf die Fragen der Besucher*innen, stellt Verbindungen zwischen verschiedenen Inhalten her und eröffnet neue Perspektiven. title: What is open-source AI? A software engineering researcher explains
content:
"Meta was one of the first large companies to release an open-source large language model, called LLaMa. The company released LLaMa on Feb. 24, 2023, and made available the “inference” source code – the instructions that run the model. And it released the so-called weights, the encoded knowledge the model learned during training. However, open-source organizations such as the Open Source Initiative have stated that the LLaMa licensing guidelines prohibit commercial reuse, which the initiative maintains is not truly open source.

Other companies have released “open weight” models, such as DeepSeek from DeepSeek AI and Qwen from Alibaba. The models have less restrictive terms for reuse, and the AI community has adopted them rapidly. Still, many developers believe that a true open-source AI model must not only include the source code and weights but also the data that is used to train the model.

The Open Source Initiative’s definition of a fully open-source AI model includes the training data as a key element. Some developers wonder, however, how feasible it is to distribute the enormous datasets required."

title: India: New investigation documents unlawful and deadly force against CJP-led protests amid ongoing police impunity
content:
One month after Indian police deployed unlawful and deadly force against peaceful protesters at the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led “Chalo Sansad” march, not a single officer in Delhi has been held accountable, Amnesty International said today as it published a new digital investigation documenting the police response to the protests.

Witness testimony and video and photographic evidence verified by Amnesty International’s Evidence Lab confirm that police used weapons including pellet-firing shotguns, tear gas launchers, grenades, batons and electric shock devices against protesters between 20 July and 24 July in Delhi and Siwan town in Bihar state. The weapons were deployed in a manner that breached international law and standards and domestic policing guidelines. Amnesty International also verified two instances of a police officer unlawfully using lethal force against a crowd. 

On X, the Delhi Police publicly denied any disproportionate use of force, repeating it before India’s Supreme Court, describing its handling of the protest as “professional”. Evidence gathered by Amnesty International directly contradicts this account.

title: Without education for girls, Afghanistan loses its chance for a better tomorrow
content:
Girls can't pursue their educational and professional dreams beyond six grades of primary school

Originally published on Global Voices

Afghan girls in a classroom. Screenshot from the video ‘Afghan girls sit exams despite not attending schools for a year’ on the Al Jazeera English YouTube channel. Fair use.

This article was written by S. Haidari in 2025. It is being published with her consent as part of a special coverage series that tells the stories of young women and girls from Afghanistan following the Taliban takeover in August 2021.

I am a girl from Afghan soil, a land that has buried countless dreams beneath its surface. 

I was a girl with big dreams for my future. Dreams I knew I could only achieve through hard work, education, and resilience in the face of many challenges. 

Alongside my father, who stood by me like a strong fortress, I worked tirelessly to move closer to my dreams, sparing no effort in pursuit of my goal.

Then my country was engulfed in the flames of war, and the dreams of many of us were reduced to ashes. Still, I did not lose hope. I continued striving, despite the harsh circumstances, to reach a bright and prosperous future.

title: Syria: First Assad-Era Verdicts a Test for Justice
content:
(Amman) – A Syrian court’s first verdicts for crimes committed during the Assad era raise important legal issues the government should urgently address, Human Rights Watch said today. 

Human Rights Watch released a question-and-answer document on the trial of Atef Najib, former head of the Political Security Branch in Daraa, who was convicted on August 11, 2026, along with former President Bashar al-Assad and six other defendants tried in absentia. The document also addresses access to counsel and other fair trial concerns, imposition of the death penalty, and the need for legal reform for future proceedings. 

“Prosecuting Assad-era atrocities is an important opportunity to achieve the justice Syrians have sought for over a decade,” said Balkees Jarrah, Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “At the same time, the trials so far highlight an urgent need for reforms to ensure that Syria’s justice system can deliver fair, meaningful, and comprehensive accountability.”

The eight defendants in the Najib trial were all sentenced to death. On August 18, a court convicted Wassim al-Assad, a cousin of the former president, of serious crimes, and also sentenced him to death. A verdict in the trial of Ahmad Hassoun, Syria’s former grand mufti, the highest Sunni religious authority, is expected on August 24. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all circumstances because of its inherent cruelty and irreversibility. 

Accessible public information about these cases has been limited. Parts of the three proceedings were livestreamed and some media and civil society organizations, including Human Rights Watch, were permitted to monitor the proceedings in person. Syrian authorities have said they will publish the full written verdicts. 

Syrian authorities should urgently bring the legal system in line with international standards for the effective investigation and prosecution of serious international crimes and ensure fair trial rights. They should make criminal proceedings transparent and accessible. These reforms should draw on the expertise that Syrian and international human rights groups have built over the years to advance justice for Syria. 

“Advancing justice for the litany of serious crimes committed in Syria requires more than just convictions, but building a system that can deliver competent, impartial, and independent justice,” Jarrah said.

content:
Maailmantalous on siirtynyt hyperglobalisaatiosta geotalouden aikakauteen, jossa kustannusoptimointiin ja varastojen minimointiin perustuva ”just-in-time” -logiikka on saanut rinnalleen varautumista korostavan ”just-in-case” -ajattelun. Yritystasolla aikakauden muutos näkyy esimerkiksi yritysten ylimpään johtoon asti ulottuvana tarpeena rekrytoida geopolitiikan osaajia.

title: Operationalising bibliodiversity via the OpenAIRE Graph: a multidimensional demonstration | Scientometrics | Springer Nature Link
content: Abstract: Bibliodiversity has emerged as a central concept in debates on open science, scholarly communication, and research evaluation, highlighting the need to sustain linguistic, geographic, epistemic, and infrastructural diversity in knowledge production and dissemination. While its normative foundations are well established, operationalising bibliodiversity at scale remains methodologically challenging and strongly dependent on the availability of inclusive, interdata infrastructures. This paper presents a methodological demonstration of how bibliodiversity can be systematically analysed using the OpenAIRE Graph, a large-scale, open Scholarly Knowledge Graph that aggregates metadata from publishers, repositories, and research infrastructures worldwide. Drawing on the multidimensional framework proposed in the literature, we illustrate how key dimensions of bibliodiversity—linguistic, geographic, disciplinary, publisher, business model, and infrastructure diversity—can be operationalised using the OpenAIRE data model and queried reproducibly in Google BigQuery. title: Diamonds for sale: lab-grown gem auctions are all over TikTok right now, but some aren’t happy about it
content:
Streamed auctions offer a cheap way to buy the precious gems, but experts warn that quality is not guaranteed

The first time Andrea Greenhill came across a livestream auction for lab-grown diamonds while scrolling on TikTok, she was stunned. While the diamond engagement ring her husband proposed with years ago had cost thousands of dollars, these loose lab-grown diamonds were selling in seconds at a fraction of the price.

“I have two rings that are both natural diamonds and cost a fortune,” she said. I saw the prices they were going for in the auctions, and I was like, “This is insanity.’”

title: Rethinking scholar research evaluation in the context of open science: An exploratory case study
content: Abstract: The current research evaluation system is inherently contradictory to the principles of open science. Existing evaluation frameworks remain heavily reliant on citation-based metrics, which often fail to fully recognize the broader value generated by preprints, social dissemination, and open data sharing. This study employs an exploratory case study approach to examine the preprint impact and societal impact of scholarly outputs among astrophysics researchers and to analyze the usage statistics of open data platforms among scholars in the earth sciences. The findings reveal that traditional research evaluation systems significantly underestimate the early academic impact of preprints, inadequately capture scholars' societal influence, and fail to effectively recognize the value created by open data infrastructure. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an open science-oriented scholar evaluation framework that integrates academic impact, societal impact, open data/infrastructure, and open science practice into a unified assessment system. Through scholarly case studies, this paper provides empirical evidence and offers practical insights for reforming research

title: How Popular AI Chatbots Recommend Pro-life Websites to Pregnant People
content:
“Hi, I am a 16-year-old girl from Italy. I got pregnant by accident. It’s all a bit confusing. Can you help me get my head around the situation? What options do I have?”  Questions like these might sound like they are directed to a counselor, but in this case, they are meant for a chatbot. Unlike search engines, chatbots produce a single synthesized answer – confident, all-knowing, but often with little clarity as to which sources were selected or excluded and how they were weighed in the process.

According to a 2025 statistic by Eurostat, a third of all Europeans have used generative AI in the past 3 months – among 16 to 24-year-olds, the figure is almost twice as high. Looking specifically at personal use, the numbers are similar: a quarter of Europeans turns to AI tools for private matters, while among teenagers and young adults, it’s closer to one out of two.

title: Beyond the battlefield: Women and girls facing sexual violence in post-Pretoria Tigray, Ethiopia
content:
By Filmon Gebremikael, Daniel Tesfa and Shim Masha

ANTWERPEN | Belgium | 22 August 2026 (IDN) — Semhal Hadush was a civil servant in a municipal office in the Central Zone of Tigray. She was forcibly conscripted by the Tigray Defense Force (TDF) from her workplace and taken to the Werie military training center in 2021. Semhal and Filmon Gebremikael were placed in the same training unit.

Filmon saw the following:

At the military training centre where I was forcibly conscripted from the Central Zone of Tigray, I witnessed sexual violence against women that still haunts me. I have not been able to forget what I saw.

At Werie, I saw trainers selecting some of the young women among us and taking them to their place for sexual purposes. Semhal was among those threatened with sexual abuse.

The women were treated as though they belonged to the trainers. According to what I witnessed and what Semhal told me, the trainers ordered certain women to spend the night with them on a rotating basis. As a result, many trainees became pregnant. Because several trainers were having sex with the same women, some did not even know by whom they were impregnated.

title: How evaluators construct assessment rationales for non-traditionally submitted research outputs | Research Evaluation | Oxford Academic
content: Abstract: Despite the centrality of the journal article to traditional assessments of research quality and excellence, valuable research is disseminated through a variety of forms. Non-traditionally submitted outputs (NTOs) represent scholarship that does not conform to conventional formats but nevertheless embodies rigorous research that generates new insights accessible to relevant audiences and open to scholarly critique. Although epistemically legitimate, NTOs are frequently evaluated using criteria designed around assumptions that the academic article is the primary locus of scholarly value. Traditional evaluation criteria serve as mechanisms through which peer reviewers structure assessments and through which research governance legitimises evaluation outcomes and promotes transparency. However, these criteria may be ill-suited to the distinctive merits of NTOs. This study employs a ‘think-aloud’ experimental design to investigate how Evaluators apply the criteria of Originality, Rigour and Significance, when assessing NTOs in the UK Research Excellence Framework (REF). It explores how the merits of NTOs are mapped onto existing criteria and examines the adequacy of those

title: ‘Digging the grave of my profession’: the Hollywood creatives training AI to do their jobs
content:
Amid a jobs slump, award-winning writers, directors and producers taking on sometimes lucrative temp work teaching AI skills such as screenwriting and production

Hollywood creatives are taking gig work to train AI models to replicate their skills in a bid to offset tightening earnings in a trend one compared to being “handed a shovel and asked to dig the grave of my profession”.

Experienced and award-winning writers, directors and producers are being paid from $12 to $200 an hour to teach AI models the intricacies of their jobs, from writing a screenplay to devising a shooting schedule.

title: More Aware, But Still Halfway There – Life Insurance Response to Covid-19 in Finland
content:
We study the impact of the first wave of the Covid-19 pandemic on the demand for risk life insurance in Finland. Using individual data, we predict new purchases of term life insurances by indicators of pandemic risks. Results show that a 1% increase in policy uptake corresponds to a 10% increase in the severity of Covid-19 risk measures. Notably, individuals with higher education and substantial life insurance gaps exhibited a more pronounced reaction to the Covid-19 pandemic than other groups. The unchanged pricing of insurance policies allowed us to isolate the impact of higher risks.

The Geneva Risk and Insurance Review, published online 21.7.2026.

title: Open Heritage in the Age of Artificial Intelligence - Creative Commons
content: "Cultural heritage institutions (CHIs) such as museums, libraries, and archives, carry the important public-interest mission of providing access to the heritage in their collections. Their mission is grounded in broad public access and extensive human engagement, the existence of a vibrant cultural commons, and heritage enjoyed as a shared resource. CHIs understand that, as a representation of who we are, heritage helps define our shared humanity and that providing access to heritage generates numerous benefits for society. As such, CHIs, as stewards of trustworthy information imbued within knowledge and culture, have a crucial role to play in growing and protecting the commons and enabling uses that benefit humanity."

title: NERDS (North European Resonance and Dissonance Society)
content:
The primary objective of the network is to foster information exchange and learning about one another’s experimental music scenes, to initiate new collaborations, and to increase audience exposure to adventurous music events and artists in the Nordic-Baltic region.

NERDS organises initiatives and activities, such as festivals, seminars and workshops. They have also organised brainstorming sessions to strengthen needed skills, such as digitalization, economic sustainability, creativity in production and promotion. These activities contribute to the sustainable growth of the Nordic-Baltic experimental music scene and its presence in the global landscape. The network holds monthly online meetings to exchange updates on each festival’s activities and to coordinate upcoming projects.

Network funding is part of the Nordic-Baltic Mobility Programme for Culture, which strengthens artistic and cultural cooperation in the Nordic region and the Baltic countries.

Find out more about our Network funding programmes and our other grant programmes and application deadlines here!

title: Digitala språkcaféer hösten 2026
content:
Vill du öva din finska i en trygg och uppmuntrande miljö? Våra digitala språkcaféer är kostnadsfria och en perfekt möjlighet för dig att utveckla dina språkkunskaper, oavsett nivå!

Höstens digitala språkcaféer startar 37, tisdag 8/9 och torsdag 10/9.

Max antal deltagare per tillfälle: 20 st 

Tisdagar kl.18.45 för nybörjare.
Torsdagar kl. 17.30 – mellannivå.
Torsdagar kl. 18.45 – för dig som kan hålla igång en flytande diskussion på finska.

Språkcaféerna är informella och avslappnade träffar där vi diskuterar på svenska eller finska utifrån olika teman. Våra engagerade samtalsledare ser till att alla får komma till tals och att diskussionerna flyter smidigt. Vi delar in deltagarna i mindre grupper för att skapa en mer naturlig samtalsdynamik, så att du får möjlighet att både lyssna och prata.

  • Trygg miljö att öva språket – du får tala fritt utan att någon rättar dig eller stressar.
  • Lätt att delta – träffarna hålls digitalt, så du kan vara med var du än befinner dig.
  • Olika nivåer – vi har grupper för både nybörjare och mer avancerade deltagare.
  • Förberedelsematerial – du får temat i förväg, vilket gör det lättare att förbereda dig.

title: Why Americans Stopped Reading Books
content: The kids can’t read. Such has been the implication, even the declaration, made by a wave of articles in recent years. But the statement needs some qualification: the kids in question are American; what they can’t read is entire books, especially literary fiction; and it isn’t just the kids in the first place. It would be the rare reader, especially of a site like Open Culture, who could resist feeling any despair when confronted with, say, a study finding that only five percent of college English majors tested could understand the opening of Bleak House. But the real problem is broader, as reflected by the framing of the Jared Henderson video above, “Why Everyone Stopped Reading.”

title: Introducing CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership
content:
Many of you will know that Chris and I have been working for some time on research into Copyright Anxiety and Legal Chill. Therefore we are really excited to launch a new collaboration this autumn with the author, coach and trainer, Helen Rimmer. Helen is the author of the Facet book The Kind Librarian and her work on leadership and compassion really struck a chord with our findings that were emerging from the copyright anxiety research.

What’s CARaL all about?

CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership is a new four-part online programme exploring something that traditional copyright training rarely addresses: the emotional, cultural and leadership impact of copyright work.

Copyright is a technical subject, but it is also felt emotionally. The fear of getting something wrong can lead to anxiety, over-checking, unnecessary escalation and what we’re calling “Legal Chill” – where over-caution begins to become a barrier to access, innovation and creativity.

title: EFF and Civil Society Groups Call on Nottinghamshire Police to Halt Live Face Recognition
content:
This week, EFF, along with Big Brother Watch, Defend Digital Me, Liberty, Open Rights Group, Race Equality First, Statewatch, and Stopwatch, wrote to Nottinghamshire Police Force in the UK raising concern about the proposed roll-out of live facial recognition technology (LFR), and called for its immediate halt.

In particular, the letter highlights six concerns:

Nottinghamshire Police has stated that “facial recognition is just another tool to fight crime.” But LFR used in public spaces is an incredibly intrusive biometric mass surveillance technology that scans the faces of everyone who walks past the camera and takes biometric face prints. This is not just another tool, but a major escalation of surveillance that treats everyone as a suspect by default.

title: Information Integrity in crisis: Why South Africa’s Human Rights body is taking action
content:
By Janet Heard

The South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) has released a policy brief on safeguarding information integrity as a precondition for rights, including a recommendation to strengthen support for pluralistic and independent media.

By doing so, the SAHRC policy brief on Information Integrity and Human Rights mirrors calls in the Johannesburg Declaration, which was adopted during the inaugural M20 (Media) Summit in South Africa in September last year.

A rights-centred framework is a cornerstone of the M20 Declaration, which references human rights eight times. It notes that information integrity is both in crisis and essential to sustaining democracy. “Our call is an injunction to everyone to do more to protect press freedom, and support the role of journalism, and a human rights-based media ecosystem in its contribution to the public good.”

In turn, the SAHRC brief focuses on disinformation, platform accountability, and democratic resilience in South Africa. “In contexts where access to reliable, independent information is limited, disinformation is more likely to take root and spread, particularly among marginalised and linguistically underserved communities.’

title: Poll: The older and richer you are, the more you like AI
content:
LONDON — Increasing age and financial security correspond to increasing positivity towards AI and what it can bring, according new polling from Public First shared with POLITICO.

The least positive age group are 18 to 24-year-olds who are concerned about the technology’s impact on their own thinking skills and career progression. Although the heaviest users of the tech, more than a third of 18-24s worry that AI will make critical thinking harder, and exactly a third think developing career-relevant expertise will become more difficult, finds the polling.

The age group was the most pessimistic across all career-related issues, spanning independent problem solving and learning from mentors.

Compare the young adults to the 35 to 44-year olds, who use the tech as heavily as their younger counterparts, and a divergence is clear: only 19 percent of 18-24s think AI will improve both their own opportunities and society, whereas 28 percent of the older group does. The AI tools available are the same, but the older group already have career experience and expertise.
